text:
Ava: Quick question — new int8 reranker bring-up on the Llama-variant shows a small +MRR on the overall set but a noticeable -NDCG@10 on the long-tail slice. Anyone started digging into formatting / candidate differences?

Mike: Can you paste the exact eval command and which slice you used?

Ava: Sure — running locally with:```
./eval \\--model rwrank-v2-int8 \\--data candidate_pool=prod_longtail \\--metrics ndcg@10 mrr \\--holdout holdout_2025-02
```

Jing: Did we change the doc truncation or concatenation order when building the candidate context? int8 builds sometimes expose tokenization edge cases.

Ava: We didn't touch the tokenizer. The only formatting change was switching to a "title-first" doc concat to cut average context length for latency. Could be that.

Sara: We should run a quick ablation: body-only vs title-first vs title+snippet on the same seed. I'll spin up small runs. :eyes: 

EvalBot: New eval job queued: job_id=ev-8421, seed=42, shards=8. Expected ETA ~1h. Link: https://ci/internal/evals/ev-8421

Leo: Also double-check the candidate generator — earlier we saw subtle score shifts when we regenerated candidates with the byte-level tokenizer for quant builds. That can change the candidate distribution and hurt NDCG on the tail.

Ava: Results from ev-8421 (holdout_2025-02):
- body-only: NDCG@10=0.287, MRR=0.412
- title-first: NDCG@10=0.259, MRR=0.418
- title+snippet: NDCG@10=0.291, MRR=0.409
So title-first increases top-heavy MRR but drops NDCG on long-tail.

Mike: Hmm — classic precision-at-top vs quality-of-rank trade. If title-first boosts early signal, it might compress scores and reorder mid/rank positions poorly. Check pairwise loss / calibration.

Jing: Also check pruning threshold: `top-k prune: k=100` for the prod pipeline. If title-first surfaces stronger top candidates, pruning could disproportionately remove good mid-rank candidates. Try k=250.

Sara: I'll run a k-sweep (100/200/250/500) + pairwise AUC and report pairwise loss deltas. If NDCG still drops, we can try reweighting pairwise pairs from the tail or adding a small hinge on rank positions.

Ava: Plan recap: Sara = k-sweep + pairwise AUC; Jing = tokenizer parity + candidate regen check; Leo = candidate generator score-distribution diff; Mike = look at pairwise loss slices. Ping me with links to runs. Thanks all :pray:
